title: Boxes and circles: collision tests
instructions:
## Did they hit?

Every frame the engine asks whether pairs of entities overlap. Write the three tests a 2D engine needs.

1. `aabbOverlap(a, b)`: two axis-aligned boxes `{x, y, w, h}` (top-left corner, width, height) overlap when they share some area; touching edges do **not** count.
2. `circleOverlap(c1, c2)`: circles `{x, y, r}` overlap when the distance between centres is less than the sum of radii. Compare squared distances; do not call `Math.sqrt`.
3. `circleInBox(c, b)`: a circle hits a box when the closest point of the box to the circle's centre is within the radius (clamp the centre to the box).
hints: Boxes do not overlap when one is entirely left, right, above or below the other: a.x + a.w <= b.x || b.x + b.w <= a.x || ...
closestX = Math.max(b.x, Math.min(c.x, b.x + b.w)); same for y; then compare the squared distance with r*r.

checks.label: No Math.sqrt in the circle tests
checks.message: Compare squared distances; a square root per pair per frame is wasted work.

realityNote: Engines run these narrow-phase tests only on pairs a broad phase (a grid or quadtree) says might collide; with hundreds of entities, testing every pair is what makes a game stutter on a low-end phone.
